title: Chapter 56 — Displacing the Incumbent: The Spec-In Strategy
intro: The displacement doctrine, the five wedges, the spec-in play, and the patient tier-one campaign.

sections.title: The Five Wedges
sections.content:
Every trade account has an incumbent supplier. To displace them, you need a wedge — a specific advantage that makes the builder or designer try you on one project.

Product availability: the incumbent does not carry a brand the designer wants to spec. Delivery reliability: the incumbent has missed delivery windows. Pricing: you can beat them on a specific package. Service: their trade rep is unresponsive. Expertise: you know more about panel-ready integration, luxury brands, or installation requirements.

sections.title: The Spec-In Play
sections.content:
The most powerful displacement strategy is the spec-in. Get a designer to specify your recommended products on a project before the builder has chosen a supplier. Once the spec is written, the builder has to source from someone who carries those specific models. If you are the only local dealer carrying that configuration, you win the project.

This requires deep designer relationships and product knowledge that exceeds the incumbent. You need to know which products are exclusive or difficult to source — those are your spec-in weapons.

sections.title: Patience
sections.content:
Displacing an incumbent takes time. The builder has an existing relationship, existing pricing, and existing habits. You will not win them with one meeting.

The patient campaign: introduce yourself, provide value without asking for business, stay visible, wait for the incumbent to make a mistake — a missed delivery, a wrong product, a slow quote — and be ready to step in. 'I heard you had a delivery issue on the Smith project. If you ever want a backup option, I am here.'

Most accounts are won not by being better — but by being ready when the incumbent stumbles.
